subject: Dedicated capacity: nightly throughput drift, observability sampling & credit request
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@argus.ai>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Argus AI Legal <legal@argus.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T08:12:00Z
Subject: Observed nightly throughput drift on reserved GPUs — request for credit + instrumentation

Marcus,

Thanks for taking this — were seeing a consistent increase in tail latency on our reserved GPU pool between 02:00-04:30 UTC over the past three weeks. Peak concurrency is within our committed range but end-to-end p95 is spiking ~2.5x compared to daytime baselines. I attached a small sample from our observability ingestion (observability-sample.csv) and a set of hourly graphs (nightly-drift-graphs.png).

Wed like to request: 1) an explanation of queueing changes overnight (any background maintenance, nightly jobs, or re-balancing events), 2) an interim credit for tokens impacted while this is investigated, and 3) guidance on a short-term instrumentation/sampling plan so we can correlate on our side.

Timing is tight: procurement is finalizing the PO this week and our finance team wants the SLA addendum clarified before signing. Can you propose concrete remediation and whether this qualifies for an SLA exception / credit?

Best,
Tom Reynolds
Director, Platform Reliability
Argus AI

Attachments: observability-sample.csv (csv stub), nightly-drift-graphs.png (image stub)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@argus.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-19T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed nightly throughput drift on reserved GPUs — request for credit + instrumentation

Tom — thanks for the clear data. Ive pulled logs for your reserved pool (pool-id: rsv-argus-eu-1) and there are two concurrent factors that match what youre seeing: a) periodic background snapshotting jobs we run across hosts between 01:30-03:00 UTC which add short-lived IO pressure on node controllers, and b) a recent scheduler tweak (rolled 3 weeks ago) that favors steady-state bin-packing to reduce daytime latency — that tweak increases transient queueing when utilization is high and many short requests arrive simultaneously.

Proposal (short term):
- We can temporarily disable the snapshotting window for your pool during your critical hours (01:30-04:30 UTC) for the next 30 days while we test alternatives.
- We will enable per-token sampling (1% sample at generation time) and stream traces to the Drive link you provided; that will give both sides enough signal to pinpoint requests that hit queueing vs kernel-level slowdowns.
- For the credit: were prepared to offer a proportional throughput credit for the affected windows in July (we estimate 4%-7% of nightly token volume based on the sample). Ben can confirm precise credit language for the addendum.

Operational asks from Argus: an exported list of typical request sizes during the window (short/medium/long) so we can reproduce. If you can share an anonymized sample (tokens + seq len buckets) that would speed the root cause work.

Ill start a short internal runbook to test disabling snapshots on your pool and will coordinate the change outside of your peak business hours. Proposed change window: 2028-07-20 00:45-01:15 UTC (rollback plan included).

—Marcus Lin
Head of Site Reliability (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference

Quoted: 
> On 2028-07-19T08:12:00Z, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@argus.ai> wrote:
> Marcus,
> Were seeing a consistent increase in tail latency...

Attachments referenced: SLA-amendment-draft-argusai.docx (draft placeholder)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@argus.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-19T12:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed nightly throughput drift on reserved GPUs — request for credit + instrumentation

Tom — appreciate the patience and the data. From a commercial perspective heres what we can do immediately while Marcus's team investigates:
- Apply a provisional credit on next invoice equal to 6% of billed tokens for the July nightly windows (this is prorated and will be reconciled once root cause is confirmed).
- Add explicit language to the dedicated capacity addendum: a temporary deviance clause for scheduled maintenance and background tasks, plus a remediation credit clause triggered by repeated p95 degradation beyond a 1.8x multiplier vs baseline.

If Argus is comfortable we can attach a one-page amendment to your PO today and sign by e-signature; legal can follow up on precise wording. Lauren, can you draft the brief addendum and drop it into the Drive folder?

Also, to reduce churn on your side, we can give you a small telemetry dashboard with the sampling stream enabled (read-only) so Argus SREs can see the same queueing signals in near real-time.

—Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

Quoted: 
> On 2028-07-19T09:03:00Z, marcus_lin@redwood.ai wrote:
> Proposal (short term):
> - disable snapshotting window for your pool ...

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@argus.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Argus AI Legal <legal@argus.ai>
Date: 2028-07-19T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed nightly throughput drift on reserved GPUs — request for credit + instrumentation

Ben / Marcus — thanks, this is the right approach. Argus legal has reviewed and is OK with a provisional credit and a short deviance clause as long as we have a measurable sampling plan and a clear rollback/notification timeline for the snapshot disable.

Two quick items:
1) Please share the telemetry dashboard link once the 1% sampling stream is live. Wed like read-only access for our SRE and one engineer from legal to spot-check traces.
2) Can Redwoods addendum language include an explicit 30-day review window (after which both parties will reconvene and either close the exception or extend remediation)?

If you can drop the one-page amendment into the Drive link and send a DocuSign link for the PO addendum, finance will route the signature today. Meeting-wise — propose a 30-minute sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC to confirm the snapshot disable window and sampling config.

Tom Reynolds
Director, Platform Reliability
Argus AI

Attachments: none
